newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ SHARES CLOSE SHARPLY WEAKER AS SENTIMENT SOURS.
newsitem.headline: NZ SHARES CLOSE SHARPLY WEAKER AS SENTIMENT SOURS.

text.p: * NZ top-40 ends 1.89 percent weaker on moderate turnover
* Rising U.S. rates frighten investors away from equities
* All eyes on U.S. retail sales data tonight
Price movements at close

New Zealand share prices closed sharply weaker on Wednesday as rising U.S. interest rates drove investors out of equities here and abroad.
The NZSE-40 Capital Index fell 47.16 points or 1.89 percent to 2,450.92 on moderate volume worth NZ$56 million.
"Mostly it is the reversal of the trend in interest rates and offshore equity markets moving lower," Tim Koller at Merrill Lynch said of the New Zealand sell-off.
Amid concerns about accelerating economic growth in the United States, U.S. interest rates have been rising and stock prices have been falling. The Dow shed 101.27 points overnight.
"It's a reversal of trend, with interest rates rising internationally these last few trading days making people just a little bit nervous about holding equities," Koller said.
Market leader Telecom was hammered 16 cents to $7.38, Carter Holt Harvey lost 12 to $3.36, and Fletcher Energy, an exceptionally strong performer in recent times, plunged 18 cents to $5.32.
Brokers said all eyes would be on U.S. retail data out tonight (NZT) to see how offshore markets reacted.
However, there was room for optimism looking out into the medium term.

Brokers noted that the market's hefty falls this week had been on only moderate volume, and they said a string of good company results on Wednesday augured well for other corporate profits as the reporting season kicked into gear.
In a troughing New Zealand economy, Tasman Agriculture, Metropolitan Lifecare and LWR Industries posted relatively healthy profits.
